situation:
You are a financial analyst at SLATE RIDGE MINERALS, a mining and materials company that extracts and processes industrial minerals for construction and battery customers. The chief financial officer (judge), part of the leadership team brought in eighteen months ago, has asked you to prepare a recommendation for the board's spring meeting.

Two bad years cost the company its dividend and about a fifth of its staff. The turnaround has worked: the mine is profitable again, and its competitive advantage is the ore grade at its main site and a delivery record customers still trust. There is enough free cash this year to do one thing well, and the board expects a recommendation on the split between paying shareholders and reinvesting.

When the dividend was suspended, the company told shareholders publicly that it would be restored as soon as the mine returned to profit. Retired workers hold most of the shares through the employee share plan, and many of them count on that payment. Restoring it now would use the year's cash and keep a promise made in front of everyone.

The alternative is reinvestment, and it comes in two parts. A processing upgrade would let the mine sell a higher-grade product, but it pays back only if a forecast of battery-mineral demand holds, and that forecast is one analyst's view of a market two years out. A funded certification and training program for the accounting and engineering staff, with membership in a professional accounting organization, would slow the loss of people to competitors who pay for it.

Either reinvestment asks the retired workers to wait another year, while restoring the dividend leaves nothing to fund the processing upgrade or the training program, and the company has been rebuilding its name as an employer since the layoffs. The chief financial officer (judge) wants your analysis of what each use of the cash is worth and a recommendation on the split. The chief financial officer (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the chief financial officer (judge) at SLATE RIDGE MINERALS. Business background is the same as the situation above. You arrived with the leadership team that has brought the mine back to profit, you made the public statement about restoring the dividend, and you have one year of free cash to allocate. You want the analyst to tell you what each use of that cash is worth to the company and to recommend the split between paying shareholders and reinvesting.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and listen to the presentation without steering it. After the presentation, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: How would you explain this to the retired workers who count on the dividend?
What should we tell them we are doing with the money instead?
